# Ākāsakathā (Kv 6.6)

**ID:** Kv 6.6
**Section:** Kathāvatthu (kv)
**Collection:** Abhidhamma
**Title (Pali):** Ākāsakathā
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/abh03m3.mul13.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Ākāsakathā* (Kv 6.6) is a doctrinal debate situated in the sixth chapter of the *Kathāvatthu*, the fifth book of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka. The discourse addresses the controversy regarding whether space (*ākāsa*) is unconditioned (*asaṅkhata*) [Karunadasa 1967]. In the course of the dialectical exchange recorded in the text, when the opponent queries whether space is conditioned (*Ākāso saṅkhato ti*), the Theravādin interlocutor responds that it should not be so designated (*Na h'evaṁ vattabbe*) [Karunadasa 1967]. This concession indicates that the notion of space debated here differs from the conditioned space-element (*ākāsadhātu*) recognized in the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī*, developing out of early canonical passages indicating that space does not rest on anything [Karunadasa 1967].

 The debational apparatus and phrasing of the *Ākāsakathā* closely mirror neighboring debates in the *Kathāvatthu* that examine whether particular categories are unconditioned or fixed, most extensively the *Paṭiccasamuppādakathā* (Kv 6.2), *Nirodhasamāpattikathā* (Kv 6.5), *Niyāmakathā* (Kv 6.1), and *Āruppakathā* (Kv 6.4), along with the *Pattikathā* (Kv 19.4), *Sāmaññaphalakathā* (Kv 19.3), and *Tathatākathā* (Kv 19.5) [DharmaNexus]. It also shares core dialectical formulas with the *Puggalakathā* (Kv 1.1) and a short passage with the *Tevijja Sutta* (DN 13) [DharmaNexus]. Across languages, DharmaNexus aligns segments of the text with the Tibetan translation of the *Saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtaviniścaya* (D3897) [DharmaNexus].
